ko.title: [마케팅 101 #12] 검색한 지 10초 후 그 광고가 어떻게 당신을 찾았는가

segments.src: > Digital marketing isn't one thing — it's three different jobs: social media goes where attention already is, search advertising catches demand at the exact moment someone types it, and content marketing earns trust long before anyone is ready to buy.
segments.tr: > 디지털 마케팅은 하나의 일이 아니다 — 세 가지의 서로 다른 일들이다: 소셜 미디어는 이미 주목받고 있는 곳으로 가고, 검색 광고는 누군가 타이핑하는 정확한 순간에 수요를 포착하며, 콘텐츠 마케팅은 누구도 아직 사려 준비되기 전에 신뢰를 얻는다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Most people picture "digital marketing" as a single blob of ads on the internet.
segments.tr: 대부분의 사람들은 "디지털 마케팅"을 인터넷상의 광고들 덩어리로 생각한다.

segments.src: It's more useful to think of it as three distinct jobs, each answering a different question about the customer.
segments.tr: 각각이 고객에 대한 다른 질문에 답하는 세 가지의 서로 다른 일으로 생각하는 것이 더 유용하다.

segments.src: **Social media marketing** answers: *how do we reach people who aren't looking for us yet?* On Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, or Reddit, nobody opened the app to shop.
segments.tr: **소셜 미디어 마케팅**은 이렇게 답한다: *어떻게 우리를 찾지 않는 사람들에게 도달할까?* 인스타그램, 틱톡, 유튜브, 링크드인, 또는 레딧에서 아무도 쇼핑하러 앱을 열지 않는다.

segments.src: They came for entertainment or connection.
segments.tr: 그들은 엔터테인먼트나 연결을 위해 왔다.

segments.src: So the ad has to earn its place in the feed — it interrupts.
segments.tr: 그래서 광고는 피드에서 자리를 얻어야 한다 — 방해한다.

segments.src: That means you pay for **attention** and target by *who someone is* (age, location, interests, past behavior, lookalikes of your existing customers).
segments.tr: 즉, 당신은 **주목**을 위해 비용을 지불하고 *누군가가 누구인지*(나이, 위치, 관심사, 과거 행동, 기존 고객과 유사한 사람들)로 타겟팅한다.

segments.src: Demand here is **latent**: you're creating want that wasn't there five seconds ago.
segments.tr: 여기서 수요는 **잠재적**이다: 당신은 5초 전에 없었던 욕구를 만들고 있다.

segments.src: **Search advertising** answers: *how do we show up when someone is already looking?* Someone types "emergency plumber Chicago" into Google.
segments.tr: **검색 광고**는 이렇게 답한다: *어떻게 누군가가 이미 찾고 있을 때 나타날까?* 누군가 구글에 "긴급 수도 배관공 시카고"를 입력한다.

segments.src: They have a problem right now.
segments.tr: 그들은 지금 문제를 가지고 있다.

segments.src: You're not creating demand — you're **harvesting** it.
segments.tr: 당신은 수요를 만드는 게 아니다 — 당신은 그것을 **수확**한다.

segments.src: That's why search clicks convert far better than social clicks, and why they cost more.
segments.tr: 그것이 검색 클릭이 소셜 클릭보다 훨씬 더 잘 전환되고, 왜 더 비싼지의 이유다.

segments.src: Here's the part most beginners get wrong: search ads are not a simple "highest bidder wins" auction.
segments.tr: 초보자들이 틀리는 부분은 다음과 같다: 검색 광고는 단순한 "최고 입찰자가 이기는" 경매가 아니다.

segments.src: Google and Bing rank ads roughly by a combination of your bid and how relevant and useful your ad and landing page are (Google calls its relevance signal **Quality Score**).
segments.tr: 구글과 빙은 광고를 대략 당신의 입찰 가격과 당신의 광고와 랜딩 페이지가 얼마나 관련성 있고 유용한지의 조합으로 순위를 매긴다 (구글은 그 관련성 신호를 **품질 점수(Quality Score)**라고 부른다).

segments.src: Simplified:
segments.tr: 단순화하면:

segments.src: Ad Rank ≈ Max Bid × Quality Score (plus other context signals)
segments.tr: Ad Rank ≈ Max Bid × Quality Score (plus other context signals)

segments.src: The practical consequence: a well-written ad pointing to a fast, relevant landing page can outrank a competitor who bids more.
segments.tr: 실제 결과: 빠르고 관련성 있는 랜딩 페이지를 가리키는 잘 작성된 광고는 더 많이 입찰하는 경쟁자보다 순위를 더 높게 차지할 수 있다.

segments.src: Relevance is a discount.
segments.tr: 관련성은 할인이다.

segments.src: **Content marketing** answers: *how do we get chosen when someone finally compares options?* Blog posts, comparison guides, newsletters, YouTube explainers, podcasts.
segments.tr: **콘텐츠 마케팅**은 이렇게 답한다: *누군가가 마침내 선택사항을 비교할 때 어떻게 선택받을까?* 블로그 포스트, 비교 가이드, 뉴스레터, 유튜브 설명 영상, 팟캐스트.

segments.src: You're not selling — you're being useful.
segments.tr: 당신은 판매하지 않는다 — 당신은 도움이 된다.

segments.src: The payoff is slow and compounding: an article that ranks in search or gets shared keeps working for months or years after you publish it, with no per-click cost.
segments.tr: 보상은 느리고 복합적이다: 검색에서 순위를 매기거나 공유되는 기사는 당신이 게시한 후 수개월 또는 수년 동안 계속 작동하며, 클릭당 비용이 없다.

segments.src: The tradeoff is that it takes time to build and is hard to attribute cleanly.
segments.tr: 트레이드오프는 구축하는 데 시간이 걸리고 깔끔하게 귀속시키기 어렵다는 것이다.

segments.src: A common way to organize all three is the **paid / owned / earned** framework:
segments.tr: 세 가지 모두를 조직하는 일반적인 방법은 **유료 / 소유 / 획득** 프레임워크이다:

segments.src: - **Paid** — you rent the audience (social ads, search ads). Fast, measurable, stops the moment you stop paying.
segments.tr: - **유료** — 당신은 청중을 임차한다 (소셜 광고, 검색 광고). 빠르고, 측정 가능하고, 지불을 멈추는 순간 멈춘다.

segments.src: - **Owned** — you control the asset (your website, blog, email list, app). Slow to build, but it's yours.
segments.tr: - **소유** — 당신은 자산을 통제한다 (당신의 웹사이트, 블로그, 이메일 리스트, 앱). 구축하는 데는 느리지만, 그것은 당신의 것이다.

segments.src: - **Earned** — others give it to you (word of mouth, press, reviews, shares). Most credible, least controllable.
segments.tr: - **획득** — 다른 사람들이 당신에게 준다 (입소문, 언론, 리뷰, 공유). 가장 신뢰할 수 있는, 가장 통제하기 어렵다.

segments.src: Healthy programs use all three.
segments.tr: 건강한 프로그램은 세 가지 모두를 사용한다.

segments.src: Paid buys you speed; owned buys you independence from ad costs; earned buys you credibility neither of the others can purchase directly.
segments.tr: 유료는 당신에게 속도를 구입한다; 소유는 광고 비용으로부터 독립성을 구입한다; 획득은 다른 둘이 직접 구입할 수 없는 신뢰도를 구입한다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 생활에서

segments.src: Say you're in Denver and your knees have been hurting after runs.
segments.tr: 당신이 덴버에 있고 달리기 후 무릎이 아프다고 말해보자.

segments.src: **Tuesday night.** You're scrolling Instagram and a 15-second Reel from a shoe brand shows a runner explaining why flat feet need stability shoes.
segments.tr: **화요일 밤.** 당신은 인스타그램을 스크롤하고 있고 신발 브랜드의 15초 릴에서 주자가 평발에는 안정성 신발이 필요한 이유를 설명한다.

segments.src: You weren't shopping.
segments.tr: 당신은 쇼핑 중이 아니었다.

segments.src: You watch it, don't click, and forget it.
segments.tr: 당신은 이를 본다, 클릭하지 않고, 잊는다.

segments.src: That's *social* — latent demand, paid for by impressions and attention.
segments.tr: 그것이 *소셜*이다 — 잠재 수요, 노출과 주목으로 지불되었다.

segments.src: **Saturday morning.** Your knees hurt again.
segments.tr: **토요일 아침.** 당신의 무릎이 다시 아프다.

segments.src: You Google "best stability running shoes flat feet."
segments.tr: 당신은 구글에 "최고의 안정성 달리기 신발 평발"을 입력한다.

segments.src: The top two results say **Sponsored**.
segments.tr: 상위 두 결과에는 **스폰서됨**이라고 표시된다.

segments.src: That's *search* — you expressed the demand, and brands paid to be there.
segments.tr: 그것이 *검색*이다 — 당신이 수요를 표현했고, 브랜드들이 거기 있으려고 비용을 지불했다.

segments.src: A retailer's ad for local running stores might cost them somewhere in the range of a few dollars per click for a term like that, because the intent is worth it.
segments.tr: 지역 런닝 스토어의 광고는 그들에게 그러한 용어에 대해 클릭당 몇 달러 범위의 비용이 들 수 있다, 의도가 그 가치가 있기 때문에.

segments.src: **Saturday afternoon.** Below the ads, you find a running store's guide: "How to Tell If You Overpronate — A 60-Second At-Home Test."
segments.tr: **토요일 오후.** 광고 아래에 런닝 스토어의 가이드를 찾는다: "과다회내인지 알아보는 방법 — 60초 자가 테스트."

segments.src: No sales pitch, just a wet-footprint test.
segments.tr: 판매 피치 없이, 그냥 젖은 발자국 테스트.

segments.src: You trust these people now.
segments.tr: 당신은 이제 이 사람들을 신뢰한다.

segments.src: That's *content* — the store paid a writer once, and that page has been earning attention ever since.
segments.tr: 그것이 *콘텐츠*이다 — 스토어가 작가에게 한 번 비용을 지불했고, 그 페이지는 계속 주목을 얻고 있다.

segments.src: **Sunday.** An ad for that exact shoe follows you across a news site and Instagram.
segments.tr: **일요일.** 그 정확한 신발에 대한 광고가 당신을 뉴스 사이트와 인스타그램 전체로 따라다닌다.

segments.src: That's **retargeting** — the store's pixel recognized you as a past visitor.
segments.tr: 그것이 **리타겟팅**이다 — 스토어의 픽셀이 당신을 과거 방문자로 인식했다.

segments.src: Creepy, effective, and legally constrained (and in California, opt-outs under CCPA/CPRA apply).
segments.tr: 으스스하고, 효과적이고, 법적으로 제한된다 (그리고 캘리포니아에서는 CCPA/CPRA 하에서의 옵트아웃이 적용된다).

segments.src: Now the business math, from the store's side.
segments.tr: 이제 비즈니스 수학, 스토어의 측면에서.

segments.src: Suppose they spend **$600/month** on search ads at a **$3.00 average CPC**:
segments.tr: 월 **$600**을 검색 광고에 **$3.00 평균 CPC**로 지출한다고 가정하자:

segments.src: 200 clicks × 4% conversion rate = 8 orders
segments.tr: 200 clicks × 4% conversion rate = 8 orders

segments.src: $600 ÷ 8 orders = $75 CAC (customer acquisition cost)
segments.tr: $600 ÷ 8 orders = $75 CAC (customer acquisition cost)

segments.src: If the average order is $120 and gross margin is 50%, each order contributes **$60** — less than the **$75** it cost to acquire.
segments.tr: 평균 주문이 $120이고 총마진이 50%라면, 각 주문은 **$60**을 기여한다 — 획득하는 데 비용이 든 **$75**보다 적다.

segments.src: That campaign *loses money on the first purchase*.
segments.tr: 그 캠페인은 *첫 번째 구매에서 돈을 잃는다*.

segments.src: It only works if that runner comes back and buys again, which is exactly why the store also invests in an email list and useful content: to lift the **lifetime value (LTV)** above the acquisition cost.
segments.tr: 그 주자가 돌아와서 다시 사는 경우에만 작동한다, 정확히 그것이 스토어가 이메일 리스트와 유용한 콘텐츠에도 투자하는 이유다: **수명 가치(LTV)**를 획득 비용 위로 올리기 위해.

segments.src: Digital marketing looks like a creative discipline, but it's decided on this arithmetic.
segments.tr: 디지털 마케팅은 창의적인 분야처럼 보이지만, 이 산술에서 결정된다.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3줄 요약

segments.src: 1. Social creates demand among people not yet looking; search harvests demand at the moment it's expressed; content builds trust that makes both cheaper over time.
segments.tr: 1. 소셜은 아직 찾지 않는 사람들 사이에서 수요를 만든다; 검색은 그것이 표현되는 순간에 수요를 수확한다; 콘텐츠는 시간이 지남에 따라 둘 다를 더 싸게 만드는 신뢰를 구축한다.

segments.src: 2. Search ad position is bid **and** relevance — better ads and landing pages effectively lower your cost.
segments.tr: 2. 검색 광고 위치는 입찰 **그리고** 관련성이다 — 더 나은 광고와 랜딩 페이지는 사실상 당신의 비용을 낮춘다.

segments.src: 3. A campaign isn't "working" because clicks are cheap; it works when acquisition cost stays below the customer's lifetime value.
segments.tr: 3. 캠페인은 클릭이 싸기 때문에 "작동하는" 게 아니다; 획득 비용이 고객의 수명 가치 아래에 머물 때 작동한다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 자가 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** Which channel primarily *harvests* existing demand rather than creating it?
segments.tr: **1.** 어느 채널이 주로 그것을 만드는 대신 기존 수요를 *수확*하는가?

segments.src: A) Instagram Reels ads  B) Google search ads  C) A brand blog  D) A podcast sponsorship
segments.tr: A) 인스타그램 릴 광고  B) 구글 검색 광고  C) 브랜드 블로그  D) 팟캐스트 스폰서십

segments.src: True or False:** In Google's ad auction, the advertiser with the highest bid always gets the top spot.
segments.tr: 참 또는 거짓:** 구글의 광고 경매에서 최고 입찰자는 항상 최상의 위치를 얻는다.

segments.src: **3.** A store spends $1,000 on ads and gets 10 new customers, each with an average order of $80 and a 50% gross margin.
segments.tr: **3.** 스토어가 광고에 $1,000을 지출하고 10명의 새로운 고객을 얻는다, 각각 평균 주문 $80과 50% 총마진을 가지고 있다.

segments.src: On the *first* purchase alone, this campaign is:
segments.tr: *첫 번째* 구매에서만, 이 캠페인은:

segments.src: A) Profitable  B) Breaking even  C) Losing money  D) Impossible to evaluate
segments.tr: A) 수익성 있는  B) 손익분기점  C) 돈을 잃는  D) 평가 불가능

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **CPC (Cost Per Click)** — What you pay each time someone clicks your ad; the standard pricing model for search advertising.
segments.tr: - **CPC(클릭당 비용)** — 누군가가 당신의 광고를 클릭할 때마다 당신이 지불하는 것; 검색 광고를 위한 표준 가격 책정 모델.

segments.src: - **CTR (Click-Through Rate)** — Clicks divided by impressions; a core measure of whether your ad actually appeals to the people seeing it.
segments.tr: - **CTR(클릭스루율)** — 클릭을 노출로 나눔; 당신의 광고가 실제로 그것을 보는 사람들에게 호소하는지 여부의 핵심 척도.

segments.src: - **Quality Score** — Google Ads' 1–10 diagnostic of expected click-through rate, ad relevance, and landing page experience; higher relevance can win better positions at a lower cost.
segments.tr: - **품질 점수** — 구글 광고의 1–10 진단으로 예상 클릭스루율, 광고 관련성, 그리고 랜딩 페이지 경험을 나타냄; 더 높은 관련성은 더 낮은 비용으로 더 나은 위치를 이길 수 있다.

segments.src: - **Retargeting (Remarketing)** — Showing ads specifically to people who already visited your site or app.
segments.tr: - **리타겟팅(리마케팅)** — 이미 당신의 사이트나 앱을 방문한 사람들에게 구체적으로 광고를 보여준다.

segments.src: - **CAC / LTV** — Customer Acquisition Cost versus Lifetime Value; the ratio that determines whether growth is actually sustainable.
segments.tr: - **CAC / LTV** — 고객 획득 비용 대 수명 가치; 성장이 실제로 지속 가능한지를 결정하는 비율.

segments.src: - **Paid / Owned / Earned Media** — Audiences you rent, channels you control, and attention others give you voluntarily.
segments.tr: - **유료 / 소유 / 획득 미디어** — 당신이 임차하는 청중, 당신이 통제하는 채널, 그리고 다른 사람들이 자발적으로 당신에게 주는 주목.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Search ads reach people who have already typed a query, meaning the need exists before the ad appears.
segments.tr: *답변: **1 — B.** 검색 광고는 이미 쿼리를 입력한 사람들에게 도달한다, 광고가 나타나기 전에 필요가 존재한다는 의미이다.

segments.src: Social and content ads mostly reach people who weren't looking.
segments.tr: 소셜 및 콘텐츠 광고는 주로 찾지 않던 사람들에게 도달한다.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Ad rank combines bid with relevance signals like Quality Score, so a more relevant advertiser can outrank a higher bidder — and often pays less per click.
segments.tr: **2 — 거짓.** 광고 순위는 품질 점수와 같은 관련성 신호를 가진 입찰을 결합하므로, 더 관련성 있는 광고주는 더 높은 입찰자보다 순위를 더 높게 차지할 수 있다 — 그리고 종종 클릭당 더 적게 지불한다.

segments.src: **3 — C, losing money.** Each order contributes $40 in gross margin ($80 × 50%), so 10 customers contribute $400 against $1,000 spent — a $600 shortfall.
segments.tr: **3 — C, 돈을 잃는다.** 각 주문은 총마진에서 $40을 기여한다 ($80 × 50%), 그래서 10명의 고객은 $1,000 지출에 대해 $400을 기여한다 — $600 부족.

segments.src: It can still be a sound investment if those customers buy again, but only repeat purchases make it so.*
segments.tr: 그 고객들이 다시 사면 여전히 건전한 투자가 될 수 있지만, 오직 반복 구매만이 그렇게 만든다.*

zh.title: [营销 101 #12] 你搜索十秒后，那个广告为什么找到了你

segments.src: > Digital marketing isn't one thing — it's three different jobs: social media goes where attention already is, search advertising catches demand at the exact moment someone types it, and content marketing earns trust long before anyone is ready to buy.
segments.tr: > 数字营销不是一件事——而是三种不同的工作：社交媒体走向注意力已经存在的地方，搜索广告在有人输入的瞬间捕获需求，而内容营销在任何人准备购买之前很久就赚取信任。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今天的概念

segments.src: Most people picture "digital marketing" as a single blob of ads on the internet.
segments.tr: 大多数人把"数字营销"想象成互联网上一堆单一的广告。

segments.src: It's more useful to think of it as three distinct jobs, each answering a different question about the customer.
segments.tr: 更有用的方式是把它看作三种不同的工作，每一种回答有关客户的不同问题。

segments.src: **Social media marketing** answers: *how do we reach people who aren't looking for us yet?* On Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, or Reddit, nobody opened the app to shop.
segments.tr: **社交媒体营销**回答的是：*我们如何触及还没有寻找我们的人？*在 Instagram、TikTok、YouTube、LinkedIn 或 Reddit 上，没有人打开应用是为了购物。

segments.src: They came for entertainment or connection.
segments.tr: 他们来这里是为了娱乐或连接。

segments.src: So the ad has to earn its place in the feed — it interrupts.
segments.tr: 所以广告必须为自己在信息流中赢得位置——它是一种打断。

segments.src: That means you pay for **attention** and target by *who someone is* (age, location, interests, past behavior, lookalikes of your existing customers).
segments.tr: 这意味着你需要支付**注意力**费用，并按*某人是谁*（年龄、位置、兴趣、过去行为、你现有客户的相似受众）来定位。

segments.src: Demand here is **latent**: you're creating want that wasn't there five seconds ago.
segments.tr: 这里的需求是**潜在的**：你正在创造五秒前不存在的欲望。

segments.src: **Search advertising** answers: *how do we show up when someone is already looking?* Someone types "emergency plumber Chicago" into Google.
segments.tr: **搜索广告**回答的是：*当有人已经在寻找时，我们如何出现？*某人在 Google 上输入"芝加哥紧急管工"。

segments.src: They have a problem right now.
segments.tr: 他们现在就有一个问题。

segments.src: You're not creating demand — you're **harvesting** it.
segments.tr: 你不是在创造需求——你是在**收获**它。

segments.src: That's why search clicks convert far better than social clicks, and why they cost more.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么搜索点击的转化效果远好于社交点击，以及为什么它们成本更高。

segments.src: Here's the part most beginners get wrong: search ads are not a simple "highest bidder wins" auction.
segments.tr: 这是大多数初学者会搞错的部分：搜索广告不是一个简单的"出价最高者获胜"的拍卖。

segments.src: Google and Bing rank ads roughly by a combination of your bid and how relevant and useful your ad and landing page are (Google calls its relevance signal **Quality Score**).
segments.tr: Google 和 Bing 大致根据你的出价以及你的广告和着陆页的相关性和实用性的组合来排列广告（Google 称其相关性信号为**质量分数**）。

segments.src: Simplified:
segments.tr: 简化版：

segments.src: Ad Rank ≈ Max Bid × Quality Score (plus other context signals)
segments.tr: Ad Rank ≈ Max Bid × Quality Score (plus other context signals)

segments.src: The practical consequence: a well-written ad pointing to a fast, relevant landing page can outrank a competitor who bids more.
segments.tr: 实际后果是：一个写得好的广告指向一个快速、相关的着陆页可以超越出价更高的竞争对手。

segments.src: Relevance is a discount.
segments.tr: 相关性是折扣。

segments.src: **Content marketing** answers: *how do we get chosen when someone finally compares options?* Blog posts, comparison guides, newsletters, YouTube explainers, podcasts.
segments.tr: **内容营销**回答的是：*当某人最终比较选项时，我们如何被选中？*博客文章、对比指南、通讯、YouTube 讲解、播客。

segments.src: You're not selling — you're being useful.
segments.tr: 你不是在销售——你是在提供帮助。

segments.src: The payoff is slow and compounding: an article that ranks in search or gets shared keeps working for months or years after you publish it, with no per-click cost.
segments.tr: 回报是缓慢而复合的：一篇在搜索中排名或被分享的文章在你发布后的几个月或几年内会继续发挥作用，没有按点击付费的成本。

segments.src: The tradeoff is that it takes time to build and is hard to attribute cleanly.
segments.tr: 权衡是它需要时间来构建，并且很难清晰地归因。

segments.src: A common way to organize all three is the **paid / owned / earned** framework:
segments.tr: 组织这三种方式的常见方法是**付费/自有/赚取**框架：

segments.src: - **Paid** — you rent the audience (social ads, search ads). Fast, measurable, stops the moment you stop paying.
segments.tr: - **付费**——你租赁受众（社交广告、搜索广告）。快速、可衡量、一旦你停止付费就停止。

segments.src: - **Owned** — you control the asset (your website, blog, email list, app). Slow to build, but it's yours.
segments.tr: - **自有**——你控制资产（你的网站、博客、电子邮件列表、应用）。构建缓慢，但它是你的。

segments.src: - **Earned** — others give it to you (word of mouth, press, reviews, shares). Most credible, least controllable.
segments.tr: - **赚取**——其他人给你的（口碑、新闻、评论、分享）。最可信，最不可控。

segments.src: Healthy programs use all three.
segments.tr: 健康的计划使用所有三种。

segments.src: Paid buys you speed; owned buys you independence from ad costs; earned buys you credibility neither of the others can purchase directly.
segments.tr: 付费为你购买速度；自有为你购买独立于广告成本的自主权；赚取为你购买其他两种都无法直接购买的信誉。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 在日常生活中

segments.src: Say you're in Denver and your knees have been hurting after runs.
segments.tr: 假设你在丹佛，你的膝盖在跑步后一直在疼。

segments.src: **Tuesday night.** You're scrolling Instagram and a 15-second Reel from a shoe brand shows a runner explaining why flat feet need stability shoes.
segments.tr: **周二晚上。**你在滚动 Instagram，一个鞋品牌的 15 秒短视频显示一位跑步者解释为什么足弓低的人需要支撑鞋。

segments.src: You weren't shopping.
segments.tr: 你不是在购物。

segments.src: You watch it, don't click, and forget it.
segments.tr: 你看了它，没有点击，然后忘记了。

segments.src: That's *social* — latent demand, paid for by impressions and attention.
segments.tr: 这就是*社交*——潜在需求，由展示次数和注意力支付。

segments.src: **Saturday morning.** Your knees hurt again.
segments.tr: **周六上午。**你的膝盖又疼了。

segments.src: You Google "best stability running shoes flat feet."
segments.tr: 你在 Google 上搜索"最好的支撑跑鞋足弓低"。

segments.src: The top two results say **Sponsored**.
segments.tr: 前两个结果显示**赞助**。

segments.src: That's *search* — you expressed the demand, and brands paid to be there.
segments.tr: 这就是*搜索*——你表达了需求，品牌付费在那里出现。

segments.src: A retailer's ad for local running stores might cost them somewhere in the range of a few dollars per click for a term like that, because the intent is worth it.
segments.tr: 零售商关于当地跑步店的广告对他们来说可能每次点击花费数美元左右，因为意图是值得的。

segments.src: **Saturday afternoon.** Below the ads, you find a running store's guide: "How to Tell If You Overpronate — A 60-Second At-Home Test."
segments.tr: **周六下午。**在广告下方，你找到了一家跑步店的指南："如何判断你是否过度内翻——60 秒在家测试。"

segments.src: No sales pitch, just a wet-footprint test.
segments.tr: 没有销售宣传，只是一个湿脚印测试。

segments.src: You trust these people now.
segments.tr: 你现在信任这些人了。

segments.src: That's *content* — the store paid a writer once, and that page has been earning attention ever since.
segments.tr: 这就是*内容*——店铺曾经付费给一位作家，那个页面从此一直在赚取注意力。

segments.src: **Sunday.** An ad for that exact shoe follows you across a news site and Instagram.
segments.tr: **周日。**那双确切的鞋的广告在新闻网站和 Instagram 中跟随你。

segments.src: That's **retargeting** — the store's pixel recognized you as a past visitor.
segments.tr: 这就是**再营销**——店铺的像素认出你是过去的访客。

segments.src: Creepy, effective, and legally constrained (and in California, opt-outs under CCPA/CPRA apply).
segments.tr: 令人毛骨悚然、有效，且受法律限制（在加州，CCPA/CPRA 的选择退出适用）。

segments.src: Now the business math, from the store's side.
segments.tr: 现在从店铺的角度看业务数学。

segments.src: Suppose they spend **$600/month** on search ads at a **$3.00 average CPC**:
segments.tr: 假设他们每月在搜索广告上花费**$600**，平均每次点击成本**$3.00**：

segments.src: 200 clicks × 4% conversion rate = 8 orders
segments.tr: 200 clicks × 4% conversion rate = 8 orders

segments.src: $600 ÷ 8 orders = $75 CAC (customer acquisition cost)
segments.tr: $600 ÷ 8 orders = $75 CAC (customer acquisition cost)

segments.src: If the average order is $120 and gross margin is 50%, each order contributes **$60** — less than the **$75** it cost to acquire.
segments.tr: 如果平均订单为 $120，毛利率为 50%，每个订单贡献**$60**——少于获取所需的**$75**。

segments.src: That campaign *loses money on the first purchase*.
segments.tr: 那个广告系列*在第一次购买时亏钱*。

segments.src: It only works if that runner comes back and buys again, which is exactly why the store also invests in an email list and useful content: to lift the **lifetime value (LTV)** above the acquisition cost.
segments.tr: 只有当那个跑步者回来再买一次时它才有效，这正是为什么店铺也投资于电子邮件列表和有用的内容：以提升**客户生命周期价值（LTV）**高于获取成本。

segments.src: Digital marketing looks like a creative discipline, but it's decided on this arithmetic.
segments.tr: 数字营销看起来像一个创意学科，但它是由这个算术决定的。

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3 行总结

segments.src: 1. Social creates demand among people not yet looking; search harvests demand at the moment it's expressed; content builds trust that makes both cheaper over time.
segments.tr: 1. 社交在还没有寻找的人中创造需求；搜索在需求被表达的瞬间收获需求；内容建立信任，使两者随着时间推移变得更便宜。

segments.src: 2. Search ad position is bid **and** relevance — better ads and landing pages effectively lower your cost.
segments.tr: 2. 搜索广告位置是出价**和**相关性——更好的广告和着陆页有效降低你的成本。

segments.src: 3. A campaign isn't "working" because clicks are cheap; it works when acquisition cost stays below the customer's lifetime value.
segments.tr: 3. 一个广告系列不是因为点击便宜就"有效"；当获取成本保持在客户生命周期价值以下时，它才有效。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测

segments.src: **1.** Which channel primarily *harvests* existing demand rather than creating it?
segments.tr: **1.**哪个频道主要*收获*现有需求而不是创造它？

segments.src: A) Instagram Reels ads  B) Google search ads  C) A brand blog  D) A podcast sponsorship
segments.tr: A) Instagram 短视频广告  B) Google 搜索广告  C) 品牌博客  D) 播客赞助

segments.src: True or False:** In Google's ad auction, the advertiser with the highest bid always gets the top spot.
segments.tr: 对或错：在 Google 的广告拍卖中，出价最高的广告主总是获得最高位置。

segments.src: **3.** A store spends $1,000 on ads and gets 10 new customers, each with an average order of $80 and a 50% gross margin.
segments.tr: **3.**一家店铺花费 $1,000 在广告上并获得 10 个新客户，每个客户平均订单为 $80，毛利率为 50%。

segments.src: On the *first* purchase alone, this campaign is:
segments.tr: 仅在*第一次*购买上，这个广告系列是：

segments.src: A) Profitable  B) Breaking even  C) Losing money  D) Impossible to evaluate
segments.tr: A) 盈利的  B) 收支平衡  C) 亏钱的  D) 无法评估

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今天的术语

segments.src: - **CPC (Cost Per Click)** — What you pay each time someone clicks your ad; the standard pricing model for search advertising.
segments.tr: - **CPC（每次点击成本）**——你每次有人点击你的广告时支付的金额；搜索广告的标准定价模式。

segments.src: - **CTR (Click-Through Rate)** — Clicks divided by impressions; a core measure of whether your ad actually appeals to the people seeing it.
segments.tr: - **CTR（点击率）**——点击数除以展示数；衡量你的广告是否真正吸引正在看到它的人的核心指标。

segments.src: - **Quality Score** — Google Ads' 1–10 diagnostic of expected click-through rate, ad relevance, and landing page experience; higher relevance can win better positions at a lower cost.
segments.tr: - **质量分数**——Google Ads 的 1-10 诊断，期望点击率、广告相关性和着陆页体验；更高的相关性可以以更低的成本获得更好的位置。

segments.src: - **Retargeting (Remarketing)** — Showing ads specifically to people who already visited your site or app.
segments.tr: - **再营销（重新营销）**——向已经访问过你的网站或应用的人展示广告。

segments.src: - **CAC / LTV** — Customer Acquisition Cost versus Lifetime Value; the ratio that determines whether growth is actually sustainable.
segments.tr: - **CAC / LTV**——客户获取成本与客户生命周期价值；决定增长是否真正可持续的比率。

segments.src: - **Paid / Owned / Earned Media** — Audiences you rent, channels you control, and attention others give you voluntarily.
segments.tr: - **付费/自有/赚取媒体**——你租赁的受众、你控制的频道、以及其他人自愿给你的注意力。

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Search ads reach people who have already typed a query, meaning the need exists before the ad appears.
segments.tr: *答案：**1 — B。**搜索广告触及已经输入查询的人，意味着需求在广告出现之前就存在。

segments.src: Social and content ads mostly reach people who weren't looking.
segments.tr: 社交和内容广告主要触及不在寻找的人。

segments.src: **2 — False.** Ad rank combines bid with relevance signals like Quality Score, so a more relevant advertiser can outrank a higher bidder — and often pays less per click.
segments.tr: **2 — 错。**广告排名结合出价和相关性信号（如质量分数），所以更相关的广告主可以超越更高的出价者——通常每次点击支付更少。

segments.src: **3 — C, losing money.** Each order contributes $40 in gross margin ($80 × 50%), so 10 customers contribute $400 against $1,000 spent — a $600 shortfall.
It can still be a sound investment if those customers buy again, but only repeat purchases make it so.*
segments.tr: 如果这些客户再次购买，它仍然可以是一个明智的投资，但只有重复购买才能使其如此。*

segments.tr: आप मांग नहीं बना रहे — आप इसे **काटाई** कर रहे हैं।

segments.src: That's why search clicks convert far better than social clicks, and why they cost more.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि सर्च क्लिक सोशल क्लिक से बहुत बेहतर रूपांतरित होते हैं, और वे अधिक क्यों खर्च करते हैं।

segments.src: Here's the part most beginners get wrong: search ads are not a simple "highest bidder wins" auction.
segments.tr: यह वह हिस्सा है जो अधिकांश शुरुआती लोग गलत समझते हैं: सर्च विज्ञापन एक सरल "सबसे बड़ा बोली लगाने वाला जीतता है" नीलामी नहीं है।

segments.src: Google and Bing rank ads roughly by a combination of your bid and how relevant and useful your ad and landing page are (Google calls its relevance signal **Quality Score**).
segments.tr: Google और Bing विज्ञापनों को आपकी बोली के संयोजन और आपके विज्ञापन और लैंडिंग पृष्ठ कितने प्रासंगिक और उपयोगी हैं, इसके द्वारा क्रमबद्ध करते हैं (Google अपने प्रासंगिकता संकेत को **गुणवत्ता स्कोर** कहता है)।

segments.src: Simplified:
segments.tr: सरलीकृत:

segments.src: Ad Rank ≈ Max Bid × Quality Score (plus other context signals)
segments.tr: Ad Rank ≈ Max Bid × Quality Score (plus other context signals)

segments.src: The practical consequence: a well-written ad pointing to a fast, relevant landing page can outrank a competitor who bids more.
segments.tr: व्यावहारिक परिणाम: एक अच्छी तरह से लिखा गया विज्ञापन जो एक तेज़, प्रासंगिक लैंडिंग पृष्ठ की ओर इशारा करता है, एक प्रतिद्वंद्वी को पीछे छोड़ सकता है जो अधिक बोली लगाता है।

segments.src: Relevance is a discount.
segments.tr: प्रासंगिकता एक छूट है।

segments.src: **Content marketing** answers: *how do we get chosen when someone finally compares options?* Blog posts, comparison guides, newsletters, YouTube explainers, podcasts.
segments.tr: **सामग्री विपणन** का उत्तर है: *जब कोई अंत में विकल्पों की तुलना करता है तो हम कैसे चुने जाते हैं?* ब्लॉग पोस्ट, तुलना मार्गदर्शन, समाचार पत्र, YouTube व्याख्याकार, पॉडकास्ट।

segments.src: You're not selling — you're being useful.
segments.tr: आप बेचना नहीं है — आप सहायक हो रहे हैं।

segments.src: The payoff is slow and compounding: an article that ranks in search or gets shared keeps working for months or years after you publish it, with no per-click cost.
segments.tr: भुगतान धीमा और संयोजन है: एक लेख जो सर्च में रैंक करता है या साझा किया जाता है, आप इसे प्रकाशित करने के बाद महीनों या वर्षों तक काम करता रहता है, कोई प्रति-क्लिक लागत के बिना।

segments.src: The tradeoff is that it takes time to build and is hard to attribute cleanly.
segments.tr: व्यापार-बंद यह है कि इसे बनाने में समय लगता है और साफ़ तरीके से जिम्मेदार ठहराना मुश्किल है।

segments.src: A common way to organize all three is the **paid / owned / earned** framework:
segments.tr: तीनों को व्यवस्थित करने का एक सामान्य तरीका **भुगतान / स्वामित्व / अर्जित** ढांचा है:

segments.src: - **Paid** — you rent the audience (social ads, search ads). Fast, measurable, stops the moment you stop paying.
segments.tr: - **भुगतान** — आप दर्शकों को किराए पर लेते हैं (सोशल विज्ञापन, सर्च विज्ञापन)। तेज़, मापने योग्य, जैसे ही आप भुगतान करना बंद करते हैं रुकता है।

segments.src: - **Owned** — you control the asset (your website, blog, email list, app). Slow to build, but it's yours.
segments.tr: - **स्वामित्व** — आप संपत्ति को नियंत्रित करते हैं (आपकी वेबसाइट, ब्लॉग, ईमेल सूची, ऐप)। बनाने में धीमा, लेकिन यह आपका है।

segments.src: - **Earned** — others give it to you (word of mouth, press, reviews, shares). Most credible, least controllable.
segments.tr: - **अर्जित** — दूसरे इसे आपको देते हैं (मुंह की बात, प्रेस, समीक्षा, साझाएं)। सबसे विश्वसनीय, कम से कम नियंत्रणीय।

segments.src: Healthy programs use all three.
segments.tr: स्वस्थ कार्यक्रम तीनों का उपयोग करते हैं।

segments.src: Paid buys you speed; owned buys you independence from ad costs; earned buys you credibility neither of the others can purchase directly.
segments.tr: भुगतान आपको गति खरीदता है; स्वामित्व विज्ञापन लागत से स्वतंत्रता खरीदता है; अर्जित आपको विश्वसनीयता खरीदता है जो अन्य में से कोई भी सीधे खरीद नहीं सकता।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की जिंदगी में

segments.src: Say you're in Denver and your knees have been hurting after runs.
segments.tr: मान लीजिए कि आप डेनवर में हैं और दौड़ने के बाद आपके घुटने दर्द करते हैं।

segments.src: **Tuesday night.** You're scrolling Instagram and a 15-second Reel from a shoe brand shows a runner explaining why flat feet need stability shoes.
segments.tr: **मंगलवार रात।** आप Instagram को स्क्रॉल कर रहे हैं और एक जूते की ब्रांड का 15-सेकंड का रील एक धावक को दिखाता है जो समझा रहा है कि सपाट पैरों को स्थिरता जूते क्यों चाहिए।

segments.src: You weren't shopping.
segments.tr: आप खरीदारी नहीं कर रहे थे।

segments.src: You watch it, don't click, and forget it.
segments.tr: आप इसे देखते हैं, क्लिक न करें, और इसे भूल जाएं।

segments.src: That's *social* — latent demand, paid for by impressions and attention.
segments.tr: वह *सोशल* है — अव्यक्त मांग, छाप और ध्यान द्वारा भुगतान की जाती है।

segments.src: **Saturday morning.** Your knees hurt again.
segments.tr: **शनिवार की सुबह।** आपके घुटने फिर से दर्द करते हैं।

segments.src: You Google "best stability running shoes flat feet."
segments.tr: आप Google "best stability running shoes flat feet." करते हैं।

segments.src: The top two results say **Sponsored**.
segments.tr: शीर्ष दो परिणाम **प्रायोजित** कहते हैं।

segments.src: That's *search* — you expressed the demand, and brands paid to be there.
segments.tr: वह *सर्च* है — आपने मांग व्यक्त की, और ब्रांड वहां होने के लिए भुगतान किया।

segments.src: A retailer's ad for local running stores might cost them somewhere in the range of a few dollars per click for a term like that, because the intent is worth it.
segments.tr: स्थानीय दौड़ने की दुकानों के लिए एक खुदरा विक्रेता का विज्ञापन उनके लिए उस तरह की एक शर्त के लिए प्रति क्लिक कुछ डॉलर की सीमा में कहीं खर्च हो सकता है, क्योंकि इरादा इसके लायक है।

segments.src: **Saturday afternoon.** Below the ads, you find a running store's guide: "How to Tell If You Overpronate — A 60-Second At-Home Test."
segments.tr: **शनिवार दोपहर।** विज्ञापनों के नीचे, आप एक दौड़ने की दुकान की गाइड पाते हैं: "How to Tell If You Overpronate — A 60-Second At-Home Test."

segments.src: No sales pitch, just a wet-footprint test.
segments.tr: कोई बिक्री पिच नहीं, बस एक गीले पैर छाप परीक्षण।

segments.src: You trust these people now.
segments.tr: आप अब इन लोगों पर विश्वास करते हैं।

segments.src: That's *content* — the store paid a writer once, and that page has been earning attention ever since.
segments.tr: वह *सामग्री* है — स्टोर ने एक बार एक लेखक को भुगतान किया, और वह पृष्ठ तब से ध्यान अर्जित कर रहा है।

segments.src: **Sunday.** An ad for that exact shoe follows you across a news site and Instagram.
segments.tr: **रविवार।** उस सटीक जूते के लिए एक विज्ञापन आपको एक समाचार साइट और Instagram पर अनुसरण करता है।

segments.src: That's **retargeting** — the store's pixel recognized you as a past visitor.
segments.tr: वह **पुनः लक्ष्यीकरण** है — स्टोर के पिक्सल ने आपको एक पिछले आगंतुक के रूप में पहचाना।

segments.src: Creepy, effective, and legally constrained (and in California, opt-outs under CCPA/CPRA apply).
segments.tr: डरावना, प्रभावी, और कानूनी रूप से विवश (और कैलिफोर्निया में, CCPA/CPRA के तहत ऑप्ट-आउट लागू होते हैं)।

segments.src: Now the business math, from the store's side.
segments.tr: अब व्यापार गणित, स्टोर की ओर से।

segments.src: Suppose they spend **$600/month** on search ads at a **$3.00 average CPC**:
segments.tr: मान लीजिए कि वे **$600/month** को सर्च विज्ञापनों पर **$3.00 average CPC** पर खर्च करते हैं:

segments.src: 200 clicks × 4% conversion rate = 8 orders
segments.tr: 200 clicks × 4% conversion rate = 8 orders

segments.src: $600 ÷ 8 orders = $75 CAC (customer acquisition cost)
segments.tr: $600 ÷ 8 orders = $75 CAC (customer acquisition cost)

segments.src: If the average order is $120 and gross margin is 50%, each order contributes **$60** — less than the **$75** it cost to acquire.
segments.tr: यदि औसत ऑर्डर $120 है और सकल मार्जिन 50% है, तो प्रत्येक ऑर्डर **$60** में योगदान देता है — अधिग्रहण करने के लिए **$75** से कम।

segments.src: That campaign *loses money on the first purchase*.
segments.tr: वह अभियान *पहली खरीद पर पैसे खो देता है*।

segments.src: It only works if that runner comes back and buys again, which is exactly why the store also invests in an email list and useful content: to lift the **lifetime value (LTV)** above the acquisition cost.
segments.tr: यह केवल तब काम करता है जब वह धावक वापस आता है और फिर से खरीदता है, जो बिल्कुल कारण है कि स्टोर एक ईमेल सूची और उपयोगी सामग्री में भी निवेश करता है: **जीवनकाल मूल्य (LTV)** को अधिग्रहण लागत से ऊपर उठाने के लिए।

segments.src: Digital marketing looks like a creative discipline, but it's decided on this arithmetic.
segments.tr: डिजिटल मार्केटिंग एक रचनात्मक अनुशासन की तरह दिखता है, लेकिन यह इस अंकगणित पर तय होता है।

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3-लाइन पुनरावृत्ति

segments.src: 1. Social creates demand among people not yet looking; search harvests demand at the moment it's expressed; content builds trust that makes both cheaper over time.
segments.tr: 1. सोशल उन लोगों के बीच मांग बनाता है जो अभी तक नहीं देख रहे हैं; सर्च उस पल पर मांग की काटाई करता है जब इसे व्यक्त किया जाता है; सामग्री विश्वास बनाती है जो समय के साथ दोनों को सस्ता बनाती है।

segments.src: 2. Search ad position is bid **and** relevance — better ads and landing pages effectively lower your cost.
segments.tr: 2. सर्च विज्ञापन स्थिति बोली **और** प्रासंगिकता है — बेहतर विज्ञापन और लैंडिंग पृष्ठ प्रभावी रूप से आपकी लागत को कम करते हैं।

segments.src: 3. A campaign isn't "working" because clicks are cheap; it works when acquisition cost stays below the customer's lifetime value.
segments.tr: 3. एक अभियान "काम" नहीं करता क्योंकि क्लिक सस्ते हैं; यह काम करता है जब अधिग्रहण लागत ग्राहक के जीवनकाल मूल्य से नीचे रहती है।

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ स्व क्विज़

segments.src: **1.** Which channel primarily *harvests* existing demand rather than creating it?
segments.tr: **1.** कौन सा चैनल मुख्य रूप से इसे बनाने के बजाय मौजूदा मांग की *काटाई* करता है?

segments.src: A) Instagram Reels ads  B) Google search ads  C) A brand blog  D) A podcast sponsorship
segments.tr: A) Instagram Reels ads  B) Google search ads  C) A brand blog  D) A podcast sponsorship

segments.src: **3.** A store spends $1,000 on ads and gets 10 new customers, each with an average order of $80 and a 50% gross margin.
segments.tr: **3.** एक स्टोर विज्ञापनों पर $1,000 खर्च करता है और 10 नए ग्राहक प्राप्त करता है, प्रत्येक $80 का औसत ऑर्डर और 50% सकल मार्जिन के साथ।

segments.tr: सिर्फ *पहली* खरीद पर, यह अभियान है:

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 आज की शर्तें

segments.src: - **CPC (Cost Per Click)** — What you pay each time someone clicks your ad; the standard pricing model for search advertising.
segments.tr: - **CPC (Cost Per Click)** — आप हर बार कुछ करते हैं जब कोई आपके विज्ञापन पर क्लिक करता है; सर्च विज्ञापन के लिए मानक मूल्य निर्धारण मॉडल।

segments.src: - **CTR (Click-Through Rate)** — Clicks divided by impressions; a core measure of whether your ad actually appeals to the people seeing it.
segments.tr: - **CTR (Click-Through Rate)** — छाप से विभाजित क्लिक; यह मापने का एक मूल माप कि क्या आपका विज्ञापन वास्तव में इसे देखने वाले लोगों को आकर्षित करता है।

segments.src: - **Quality Score** — Google Ads' 1–10 diagnostic of expected click-through rate, ad relevance, and landing page experience; higher relevance can win better positions at a lower cost.
segments.tr: - **Quality Score** — Google Ads' 1–10 निदान अपेक्षित क्लिक-थ्रू दर, विज्ञापन प्रासंगिकता, और लैंडिंग पृष्ठ अनुभव; उच्च प्रासंगिकता कम लागत पर बेहतर पदों को जीत सकती है।

segments.src: - **Retargeting (Remarketing)** — Showing ads specifically to people who already visited your site or app.
segments.tr: - **Retargeting (Remarketing)** — उन लोगों को विज्ञापन दिखाना जो पहले से ही आपकी साइट या ऐप पर गए हैं।

segments.src: - **CAC / LTV** — Customer Acquisition Cost versus Lifetime Value; the ratio that determines whether growth is actually sustainable.
segments.tr: - **CAC / LTV** — ग्राहक अधिग्रहण लागत बनाम जीवनकाल मूल्य; अनुपात जो निर्धारित करता है कि क्या वृद्धि वास्तव में टिकाऊ है।

segments.src: - **Paid / Owned / Earned Media** — Audiences you rent, channels you control, and attention others give you voluntarily.
segments.tr: - **Paid / Owned / Earned Media** — दर्शक जो आप किराए पर लेते हैं, चैनल जो आप नियंत्रित करते हैं, और ध्यान जो दूसरे आपको स्वेच्छा से देते हैं।

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Search ads reach people who have already typed a query, meaning the need exists before the ad appears.
segments.tr: *Answers: **1 — B.** सर्च विज्ञापन उन लोगों तक पहुंचते हैं जिन्होंने पहले से ही एक क्वेरी टाइप की है, जिसका अर्थ है कि विज्ञापन दिखाई देने से पहले आवश्यकता मौजूद है।

segments.src: Social and content ads mostly reach people who weren't looking.
segments.tr: सोशल और सामग्री विज्ञापन ज्यादातर उन लोगों तक पहुंचते हैं जो नहीं देख रहे थे।

segments.src: **2 — False.** Ad rank combines bid with relevance signals like Quality Score, so a more relevant advertiser can outrank a higher bidder — and often pays less per click.
segments.tr: **2 — False.** विज्ञापन रैंक बोली को गुणवत्ता स्कोर जैसे प्रासंगिकता संकेतों के साथ जोड़ता है, इसलिए एक अधिक प्रासंगिक विज्ञापनदाता एक उच्च बोली देने वाले को पीछे छोड़ सकता है — और अक्सर प्रति क्लिक कम भुगतान करता है।

segments.src: **3 — C, losing money.** Each order contributes $40 in gross margin ($80 × 50%), so 10 customers contribute $400 against $1,000 spent — a $600 shortfall.
segments.tr: **3 — C, losing money.** प्रत्येक ऑर्डर सकल मार्जिन में $40 योगदान देता है ($80 × 50%), इसलिए 10 ग्राहक $1,000 खर्च के विरुद्ध $400 में योगदान देते हैं — $600 की कमी।

segments.src: It can still be a sound investment if those customers buy again, but only repeat purchases make it so.*

es.title: [Marketing 101 #12] Por Qué Ese Anuncio Te Encontró Diez Segundos Después de que Buscaste

segments.src: > Digital marketing isn't one thing — it's three different jobs: social media goes where attention already is, search advertising catches demand at the exact moment someone types it, and content marketing earns trust long before anyone is ready to buy.
segments.tr: > El marketing digital no es una sola cosa — son tres trabajos distintos: las redes sociales van donde ya hay atención, la publicidad de búsqueda capta demanda en el momento exacto en que alguien la escribe, y el marketing de contenidos gana confianza mucho antes de que alguien esté listo para comprar.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El Concepto de Hoy

segments.src: Most people picture "digital marketing" as a single blob of ads on the internet.
segments.tr: La mayoría de las personas imaginan el "marketing digital" como un solo bloque de anuncios en internet.

segments.src: It's more useful to think of it as three distinct jobs, each answering a different question about the customer.
segments.tr: Es más útil pensar en ello como tres trabajos distintos, cada uno respondiendo una pregunta diferente sobre el cliente.

segments.src: **Social media marketing** answers: *how do we reach people who aren't looking for us yet?* On Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, or Reddit, nobody opened the app to shop.
segments.tr: **El marketing en redes sociales** responde: *¿cómo llegamos a personas que aún no nos buscan?* En Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn o Reddit, nadie abrió la aplicación para comprar.

segments.src: They came for entertainment or connection.
segments.tr: Vinieron para entretenerse o conectar.

segments.src: So the ad has to earn its place in the feed — it interrupts.
segments.tr: Entonces el anuncio tiene que ganarse su lugar en el feed — interrumpe.

segments.src: That means you pay for **attention** and target by *who someone is* (age, location, interests, past behavior, lookalikes of your existing customers).
segments.tr: Esto significa que pagas por **atención** y diriges a *quién es alguien* (edad, ubicación, intereses, comportamiento anterior, perfiles similares a los de tus clientes existentes).

segments.src: Demand here is **latent**: you're creating want that wasn't there five seconds ago.
segments.tr: La demanda aquí es **latente**: estás creando un deseo que no existía hace cinco segundos.

segments.src: **Search advertising** answers: *how do we show up when someone is already looking?* Someone types "emergency plumber Chicago" into Google.
segments.tr: **La publicidad de búsqueda** responde: *¿cómo aparecemos cuando alguien ya está buscando?* Alguien escribe "fontanero de emergencia Chicago" en Google.

segments.src: They have a problem right now.
segments.tr: Tienen un problema ahora mismo.

segments.src: You're not creating demand — you're **harvesting** it.
segments.tr: No estás creando demanda — la estás **cosechando**.

segments.src: That's why search clicks convert far better than social clicks, and why they cost more.
segments.tr: Por eso los clics de búsqueda se convierten mucho mejor que los clics de redes sociales, y por eso cuestan más.

segments.src: Here's the part most beginners get wrong: search ads are not a simple "highest bidder wins" auction.
segments.tr: Aquí está la parte que la mayoría de los principiantes entienden mal: los anuncios de búsqueda no son una subasta simple "gana el postor más alto".

segments.src: Google and Bing rank ads roughly by a combination of your bid and how relevant and useful your ad and landing page are (Google calls its relevance signal **Quality Score**).
segments.tr: Google y Bing clasifican los anuncios aproximadamente según una combinación de tu puja y qué tan relevantes y útiles son tu anuncio y página de destino (Google llama a su señal de relevancia **Puntuación de Calidad**).

segments.src: Simplified:
segments.tr: Simplificado:

segments.src: Ad Rank ≈ Max Bid × Quality Score (plus other context signals)
segments.tr: Ad Rank ≈ Max Bid × Quality Score (plus other context signals)

segments.src: The practical consequence: a well-written ad pointing to a fast, relevant landing page can outrank a competitor who bids more.
segments.tr: La consecuencia práctica: un anuncio bien escrito que apunta a una página de destino rápida y relevante puede superar a un competidor que puja más.

segments.src: Relevance is a discount.
segments.tr: La relevancia es un descuento.

segments.src: **Content marketing** answers: *how do we get chosen when someone finally compares options?* Blog posts, comparison guides, newsletters, YouTube explainers, podcasts.
segments.tr: **El marketing de contenidos** responde: *¿cómo nos eligen cuando alguien finalmente compara opciones?* Publicaciones de blog, guías de comparación, boletines, explicadores de YouTube, podcasts.

segments.src: You're not selling — you're being useful.
segments.tr: No estás vendiendo — estás siendo útil.

segments.src: The payoff is slow and compounding: an article that ranks in search or gets shared keeps working for months or years after you publish it, with no per-click cost.
segments.tr: La recompensa es lenta y compuesta: un artículo que se clasifica en la búsqueda o se comparte sigue funcionando durante meses o años después de que lo publiques, sin costo por clic.

segments.src: The tradeoff is that it takes time to build and is hard to attribute cleanly.
segments.tr: La compensación es que toma tiempo construirlo y es difícil atribuirlo limpiamente.

segments.src: A common way to organize all three is the **paid / owned / earned** framework:
segments.tr: Una forma común de organizar los tres es el marco **pagado / propio / ganado**:

segments.src: - **Paid** — you rent the audience (social ads, search ads). Fast, measurable, stops the moment you stop paying.
segments.tr: - **Pagado** — alquilas la audiencia (anuncios sociales, anuncios de búsqueda). Rápido, medible, se detiene en el momento en que dejas de pagar.

segments.src: - **Owned** — you control the asset (your website, blog, email list, app). Slow to build, but it's yours.
segments.tr: - **Propio** — controlas el activo (tu sitio web, blog, lista de correo electrónico, aplicación). Lento de construir, pero es tuyo.

segments.src: - **Earned** — others give it to you (word of mouth, press, reviews, shares). Most credible, least controllable.
segments.tr: - **Ganado** — otros te lo dan (boca a boca, prensa, reseñas, compartidas). Más creíble, menos controlable.

segments.src: Healthy programs use all three.
segments.tr: Los programas saludables usan los tres.

segments.src: Paid buys you speed; owned buys you independence from ad costs; earned buys you credibility neither of the others can purchase directly.
segments.tr: Lo pagado te compra velocidad; lo propio te compra independencia de los costos de anuncios; lo ganado te compra credibilidad que ninguno de los otros puede comprar directamente.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la Vida Cotidiana

segments.src: Say you're in Denver and your knees have been hurting after runs.
segments.tr: Digamos que estás en Denver y tus rodillas han estado doliéndote después de correr.

segments.src: **Tuesday night.** You're scrolling Instagram and a 15-second Reel from a shoe brand shows a runner explaining why flat feet need stability shoes.
segments.tr: **Martes por la noche.** Estás desplazándote por Instagram y un Reel de 15 segundos de una marca de zapatos muestra a un corredor explicando por qué los pies planos necesitan zapatos estables.

segments.src: You weren't shopping.
segments.tr: No estabas comprando.

segments.src: You watch it, don't click, and forget it.
segments.tr: Lo ves, no haces clic y lo olvidas.

segments.src: That's *social* — latent demand, paid for by impressions and attention.
segments.tr: Eso es *social* — demanda latente, pagada por impresiones y atención.

segments.src: **Saturday morning.** Your knees hurt again.
segments.tr: **Sábado por la mañana.** Tus rodillas vuelven a doler.

segments.src: You Google "best stability running shoes flat feet."
segments.tr: Buscas en Google "mejores zapatos para correr estables pies planos".

segments.src: The top two results say **Sponsored**.
segments.tr: Los dos primeros resultados dicen **Patrocinado**.

segments.src: That's *search* — you expressed the demand, and brands paid to be there.
segments.tr: Eso es *búsqueda* — expresaste la demanda, y las marcas pagaron para estar allí.

segments.src: A retailer's ad for local running stores might cost them somewhere in the range of a few dollars per click for a term like that, because the intent is worth it.
segments.tr: Un anuncio de un minorista para tiendas locales de running podría costarles en el rango de unos pocos dólares por clic para un término como ese, porque la intención vale la pena.

segments.src: **Saturday afternoon.** Below the ads, you find a running store's guide: "How to Tell If You Overpronate — A 60-Second At-Home Test."
segments.tr: **Sábado por la tarde.** Debajo de los anuncios, encuentras una guía de una tienda de running: "Cómo Saber Si Overpronás — Una Prueba Casera de 60 Segundos".

segments.src: No sales pitch, just a wet-footprint test.
segments.tr: Sin argumento de venta, solo una prueba de huella mojada.

segments.src: You trust these people now.
segments.tr: Ahora confías en estas personas.

segments.src: That's *content* — the store paid a writer once, and that page has been earning attention ever since.
segments.tr: Eso es *contenido* — la tienda pagó a un escritor una vez, y esa página ha estado ganando atención desde entonces.

segments.src: **Sunday.** An ad for that exact shoe follows you across a news site and Instagram.
segments.tr: **Domingo.** Un anuncio de ese zapato exacto te sigue en un sitio de noticias e Instagram.

segments.src: That's **retargeting** — the store's pixel recognized you as a past visitor.
segments.tr: Eso es **retargeting** — el píxel de la tienda te reconoció como un visitante anterior.

segments.src: Creepy, effective, and legally constrained (and in California, opt-outs under CCPA/CPRA apply).
segments.tr: Espeluznante, efectivo y legalmente restringido (y en California, se aplican exclusiones bajo CCPA/CPRA).

segments.src: Now the business math, from the store's side.
segments.tr: Ahora las matemáticas del negocio, desde el lado de la tienda.

segments.src: Suppose they spend **$600/month** on search ads at a **$3.00 average CPC**:
segments.tr: Supongamos que gastan **$600/mes** en anuncios de búsqueda a un **CPC promedio de $3.00**:

segments.src: 200 clicks × 4% conversion rate = 8 orders
segments.tr: 200 clicks × 4% conversion rate = 8 orders

segments.src: $600 ÷ 8 orders = $75 CAC (customer acquisition cost)
segments.tr: $600 ÷ 8 orders = $75 CAC (customer acquisition cost)

segments.src: If the average order is $120 and gross margin is 50%, each order contributes **$60** — less than the **$75** it cost to acquire.
segments.tr: Si el pedido promedio es $120 y el margen bruto es 50%, cada pedido contribuye **$60** — menos que los **$75** que costó adquirir.

segments.src: That campaign *loses money on the first purchase*.
segments.tr: Esa campaña *pierde dinero en la primera compra*.

segments.src: It only works if that runner comes back and buys again, which is exactly why the store also invests in an email list and useful content: to lift the **lifetime value (LTV)** above the acquisition cost.
segments.tr: Solo funciona si ese corredor vuelve y compra de nuevo, que es exactamente por qué la tienda también invierte en una lista de correo y contenido útil: para elevar el **valor de vida (LTV)** por encima del costo de adquisición.

segments.src: Digital marketing looks like a creative discipline, but it's decided on this arithmetic.
segments.tr: El marketing digital parece una disciplina creativa, pero se decide en esta aritmética.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen de 3 Líneas

segments.src: 1. Social creates demand among people not yet looking; search harvests demand at the moment it's expressed; content builds trust that makes both cheaper over time.
segments.tr: 1. Las redes sociales crean demanda entre personas que aún no buscan; la búsqueda cosecha demanda en el momento en que se expresa; el contenido construye confianza que hace ambos más baratos con el tiempo.

segments.src: 2. Search ad position is bid **and** relevance — better ads and landing pages effectively lower your cost.
segments.tr: 2. La posición del anuncio de búsqueda es puja **y** relevancia — anuncios mejores y páginas de destino reducen efectivamente tu costo.

segments.src: 3. A campaign isn't "working" because clicks are cheap; it works when acquisition cost stays below the customer's lifetime value.
segments.tr: 3. Una campaña no está "funcionando" porque los clics son baratos; funciona cuando el costo de adquisición se mantiene por debajo del valor de vida del cliente.

segments.tr: ## ✅ Autoevaluación

segments.src: **1.** Which channel primarily *harvests* existing demand rather than creating it?
segments.tr: **1.** ¿Qué canal principalmente *cosecha* la demanda existente en lugar de crearla?

segments.tr: A) Anuncios de Instagram Reels  B) Anuncios de búsqueda de Google  C) Un blog de marca  D) Un patrocinio de podcast

segments.tr: Verdadero o Falso:** En la subasta de anuncios de Google, el anunciante con la puja más alta siempre obtiene el lugar superior.

segments.src: **3.** A store spends $1,000 on ads and gets 10 new customers, each with an average order of $80 and a 50% gross margin.
segments.tr: **3.** Una tienda gasta $1.000 en anuncios y obtiene 10 nuevos clientes, cada uno con un pedido promedio de $80 y un margen bruto del 50%.

segments.src: On the *first* purchase alone, this campaign is:
segments.tr: Solo en la *primera* compra, esta campaña es:

segments.src: A) Profitable  B) Breaking even  C) Losing money  D) Impossible to evaluate
segments.tr: A) Rentable  B) En equilibrio  C) Perdiendo dinero  D) Imposible de evaluar

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Términos de Hoy

segments.src: - **CPC (Cost Per Click)** — What you pay each time someone clicks your ad; the standard pricing model for search advertising.
segments.tr: - **CPC (Costo Por Clic)** — Lo que pagas cada vez que alguien hace clic en tu anuncio; el modelo de precios estándar para publicidad de búsqueda.

segments.src: - **CTR (Click-Through Rate)** — Clicks divided by impressions; a core measure of whether your ad actually appeals to the people seeing it.
segments.tr: - **CTR (Tasa de Clics)** — Clics divididos por impresiones; una medida central de si tu anuncio realmente atrae a las personas que lo ven.

segments.src: - **Quality Score** — Google Ads' 1–10 diagnostic of expected click-through rate, ad relevance, and landing page experience; higher relevance can win better positions at a lower cost.
segments.tr: - **Puntuación de Calidad** — Diagnóstico de 1–10 de Google Ads de la tasa de clics esperada, relevancia del anuncio y experiencia de página de destino; una relevancia más alta puede ganar mejores posiciones a un menor costo.

segments.src: - **Retargeting (Remarketing)** — Showing ads specifically to people who already visited your site or app.
segments.tr: - **Retargeting (Remarketing)** — Mostrar anuncios específicamente a personas que ya visitaron tu sitio o aplicación.

segments.src: - **CAC / LTV** — Customer Acquisition Cost versus Lifetime Value; the ratio that determines whether growth is actually sustainable.
segments.tr: - **CAC / LTV** — Costo de Adquisición de Cliente versus Valor de Vida; la relación que determina si el crecimiento es realmente sostenible.

segments.src: - **Paid / Owned / Earned Media** — Audiences you rent, channels you control, and attention others give you voluntarily.
segments.tr: - **Medios Pagados / Propios / Ganados** — Audiencias que alquilas, canales que controlas y atención que otros te dan voluntariamente.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Search ads reach people who have already typed a query, meaning the need exists before the ad appears.
segments.tr: *Respuestas: **1 — B.** Los anuncios de búsqueda llegan a personas que ya han escrito una consulta, lo que significa que la necesidad existe antes de que aparezca el anuncio.

segments.src: Social and content ads mostly reach people who weren't looking.
segments.tr: Los anuncios de redes sociales y contenido principalmente llegan a personas que no estaban buscando.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Ad rank combines bid with relevance signals like Quality Score, so a more relevant advertiser can outrank a higher bidder — and often pays less per click.
segments.tr: **2 — Falso.** La clasificación de anuncios combina la puja con señales de relevancia como Puntuación de Calidad, por lo que un anunciante más relevante puede superar a un postor más alto — y a menudo paga menos por clic.

segments.src: **3 — C, losing money.** Each order contributes $40 in gross margin ($80 × 50%), so 10 customers contribute $400 against $1,000 spent — a $600 shortfall.
segments.tr: **3 — C, perdiendo dinero.** Cada pedido contribuye $40 en margen bruto ($80 × 50%), entonces 10 clientes contribuyen $400 contra $1.000 gastados — un déficit de $600.

segments.src: It can still be a sound investment if those customers buy again, but only repeat purchases make it so.*
segments.tr: Aún puede ser una inversión sólida si esos clientes compran de nuevo, pero solo las compras repetidas lo hacen así.*

segments.src: - **Earned** — others give it to you (word of mouth, press, reviews, shares). Most credible, least controllable.
segments.tr: - **مكتسب** — يعطيه الآخرون لك (كلام من الفم إلى الفم والصحافة والتقييمات والمشاركات). الأكثر مصداقية والأقل قابلية للتحكم.

segments.src: Healthy programs use all three.
segments.tr: تستخدم البرامج الصحية الثلاثة جميعاً.

segments.src: Paid buys you speed; owned buys you independence from ad costs; earned buys you credibility neither of the others can purchase directly.
segments.tr: يشتري المدفوع لك السرعة؛ يشتري المملوك لك الاستقلالية عن تكاليف الإعلانات؛ يشتري المكتسب لك المصداقية التي لا يستطيع الآخران شراءها بشكل مباشر.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## في الحياة اليومية

segments.src: Say you're in Denver and your knees have been hurting after runs.
segments.tr: لنفترض أنك في دنفر وركبتاك تؤلمانك بعد الركض.

segments.src: **Tuesday night.** You're scrolling Instagram and a 15-second Reel from a shoe brand shows a runner explaining why flat feet need stability shoes.
segments.tr: **مساء يوم الثلاثاء.** أنت تتصفح Instagram ورول مدته 15 ثانية من علامة حذاء تعرض عداءً يشرح لماذا تحتاج الأقدام المسطحة إلى أحذية مستقرة.

segments.src: You weren't shopping.
segments.tr: لم تكن تتسوق.

segments.src: You watch it, don't click, and forget it.
segments.tr: تشاهده ولا تنقر عليه وتنساه.

segments.src: That's *social* — latent demand, paid for by impressions and attention.
segments.tr: هذا *التواصل الاجتماعي* — الطلب الكامن، مدفوع بالانطباعات والاهتمام.

segments.src: **Saturday morning.** Your knees hurt again.
segments.tr: **صباح يوم السبت.** ركبتاك تؤلمانك مرة أخرى.

segments.src: You Google "best stability running shoes flat feet."
segments.tr: تبحث في Google عن "أفضل أحذية جري مستقرة للأقدام المسطحة".

segments.src: The top two results say **Sponsored**.
segments.tr: أفضل نتيجتين تقولان **برعاية**.

segments.src: That's *search* — you expressed the demand, and brands paid to be there.
segments.tr: هذا *البحث* — لقد عبرت عن الطلب والعلامات التجارية دفعت لتكون هناك.

segments.src: A retailer's ad for local running stores might cost them somewhere in the range of a few dollars per click for a term like that, because the intent is worth it.
segments.tr: قد تكلف إعلانة بائع التجزئة لمتاجر الجري المحلية بضعة دولارات في المتوسط لكل نقرة لمصطلح مثل هذا، لأن النية تستحق ذلك.

segments.src: **Saturday afternoon.** Below the ads, you find a running store's guide: "How to Tell If You Overpronate — A 60-Second At-Home Test."
segments.tr: **بعد ظهر يوم السبت.** تحت الإعلانات، تجد دليل متجر الجري: "كيفية معرفة ما إذا كنت تبالغ في الإمالة — اختبار منزلي مدته 60 ثانية".

segments.src: No sales pitch, just a wet-footprint test.
segments.tr: بدون خطاب مبيعات، فقط اختبار بصمة القدم الرطبة.

segments.src: You trust these people now.
segments.tr: أنت تثق بهؤلاء الناس الآن.

segments.src: That's *content* — the store paid a writer once, and that page has been earning attention ever since.
segments.tr: هذا *المحتوى* — دفع المتجر لكاتب مرة واحدة، والصفحة تكسب الاهتمام منذ ذلك الحين.

segments.src: **Sunday.** An ad for that exact shoe follows you across a news site and Instagram.
segments.tr: **الأحد.** إعلان لذلك الحذاء بالضبط يتابعك عبر موقع أخبار و Instagram.

segments.src: That's **retargeting** — the store's pixel recognized you as a past visitor.
segments.tr: هذا **استهداف إعادة الاستهداف** — بكسل المتجر اعترف بك كزائر سابق.

segments.src: Creepy, effective, and legally constrained (and in California, opt-outs under CCPA/CPRA apply).
segments.tr: مرعب وفعال وقانوني مقيد (وفي كاليفورنيا، تنطبق خيارات الرفض بموجب CCPA/CPRA).

segments.src: Now the business math, from the store's side.
segments.tr: الآن رياضيات الأعمال، من جانب المتجر.

segments.src: Suppose they spend **$600/month** on search ads at a **$3.00 average CPC**:
segments.tr: لنفترض أنهم ينفقون **$600/month** على إعلانات البحث بمتوسط **$3.00 CPC**:

segments.tr: 200 clicks × 4% conversion rate = 8 orders

segments.src: $600 ÷ 8 orders = $75 CAC (customer acquisition cost)
segments.tr: $600 ÷ 8 orders = $75 CAC (customer acquisition cost)

segments.src: If the average order is $120 and gross margin is 50%, each order contributes **$60** — less than the **$75** it cost to acquire.
segments.tr: إذا كان متوسط الطلب $120 والهامش الإجمالي 50%، فكل طلب يساهم بـ **$60** — أقل من **$75** التي كلفت الاستحواذ عليها.

segments.src: That campaign *loses money on the first purchase*.
segments.tr: هذه الحملة *تخسر المال عند الشراء الأول*.

segments.src: It only works if that runner comes back and buys again, which is exactly why the store also invests in an email list and useful content: to lift the **lifetime value (LTV)** above the acquisition cost.
segments.tr: يعمل فقط إذا عاد هذا العداء واشترى مرة أخرى، وهذا بالضبط السبب في أن المتجر يستثمر أيضاً في قائمة بريد إلكترونية ومحتوى مفيد: لرفع **القيمة الدائمة (LTV)** فوق تكلفة الاستحواذ.

segments.src: Digital marketing looks like a creative discipline, but it's decided on this arithmetic.
segments.tr: يبدو التسويق الرقمي وكأنه تخصص إبداعي، لكنه يتقرر بناءً على هذه الحسابات.

segments.src: ## 3-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## تلخيص 3 أسطر

segments.src: 1. Social creates demand among people not yet looking; search harvests demand at the moment it's expressed; content builds trust that makes both cheaper over time.
segments.tr: 1. التواصل الاجتماعي ينشئ طلباً بين الأشخاص الذين لا يبحثون حتى الآن؛ البحث يجني الطلب في اللحظة التي يتم التعبير عنها؛ المحتوى يبني الثقة التي تجعل كليهما أرخص بمرور الوقت.

segments.src: 2. Search ad position is bid **and** relevance — better ads and landing pages effectively lower your cost.
segments.tr: 2. موضع الإعلان البحثي هو العرض **و** الملاءمة — الإعلانات الأفضل وصفحات الهبوط تخفض فعلياً تكلفتك.

segments.src: 3. A campaign isn't "working" because clicks are cheap; it works when acquisition cost stays below the customer's lifetime value.
segments.tr: 3. لا تعمل الحملة لأن النقرات رخيصة؛ تعمل عندما تبقى تكلفة الاستحواذ أقل من القيمة الدائمة للعميل.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **CPC (Cost Per Click)** — What you pay each time someone clicks your ad; the standard pricing model for search advertising.
segments.tr: - **CPC (تكلفة لكل نقرة)** — ما تدفعه في كل مرة ينقر فيها شخص ما على إعلانك؛ نموذج التسعير القياسي للإعلانات البحثية.

segments.src: - **CTR (Click-Through Rate)** — Clicks divided by impressions; a core measure of whether your ad actually appeals to the people seeing it.
segments.tr: - **CTR (معدل النقر عبر)** — النقرات مقسومة على الانطباعات؛ مقياس أساسي لما إذا كان إعلانك يجذب الأشخاص الذين يرونه فعلياً.

segments.src: - **Quality Score** — Google Ads' 1–10 diagnostic of expected click-through rate, ad relevance, and landing page experience; higher relevance can win better positions at a lower cost.
segments.tr: - **درجة الجودة** — تشخيص Google Ads من 1 إلى 10 لمعدل النقر المتوقع وملاءمة الإعلان وتجربة صفحة الهبوط؛ الملاءمة الأعلى يمكن أن تفوز بمواضع أفضل بتكلفة أقل.

segments.src: - **Retargeting (Remarketing)** — Showing ads specifically to people who already visited your site or app.
segments.tr: - **استهداف إعادة الاستهداف (إعادة التسويق)** — عرض إعلانات محددة للأشخاص الذين زاروا موقعك أو تطبيقك بالفعل.

segments.src: - **CAC / LTV** — Customer Acquisition Cost versus Lifetime Value; the ratio that determines whether growth is actually sustainable.
segments.tr: - **CAC / LTV** — تكلفة اكتساب العميل مقابل القيمة الدائمة؛ النسبة التي تحدد ما إذا كان النمو مستدام فعلاً.

segments.src: - **Paid / Owned / Earned Media** — Audiences you rent, channels you control, and attention others give you voluntarily.
segments.tr: - **الوسائط المدفوعة / المملوكة / المكتسبة** — الجمهور الذي تستأجره والقنوات التي تتحكم فيها والاهتمام الذي يعطيه الآخرون لك طواعية.

segments.src: *Answers: **1 — B.** Search ads reach people who have already typed a query, meaning the need exists before the ad appears.
segments.tr: *الإجابات: **1 — B.** تصل إعلانات البحث إلى الأشخاص الذين كتبوا استعلاماً بالفعل، مما يعني أن الحاجة موجودة قبل ظهور الإعلان.

segments.src: Social and content ads mostly reach people who weren't looking.
segments.tr: تصل إعلانات التواصل الاجتماعي والمحتوى بشكل أساسي إلى الأشخاص الذين لم يكونوا يبحثون.

segments.src: **2 — False.** Ad rank combines bid with relevance signals like Quality Score, so a more relevant advertiser can outrank a higher bidder — and often pays less per click.
segments.tr: **2 — خطأ.** يجمع ترتيب الإعلان العرض مع إشارات الملاءمة مثل درجة الجودة، لذلك يمكن لمعلن أكثر ملاءمة أن يتفوق على عارض أعلى — وغالباً ما يدفع أقل لكل نقرة.

segments.src: **3 — C, losing money.** Each order contributes $40 in gross margin ($80 × 50%), so 10 customers contribute $400 against $1,000 spent — a $600 shortfall.
segments.tr: **3 — C، خسارة المال.** يساهم كل طلب بـ $40 في الهامش الإجمالي ($80 × 50%)، لذلك يساهم 10 عملاء بـ $400 مقابل $1,000 ينفق — نقص قدره $600.

segments.src: It can still be a sound investment if those customers buy again, but only repeat purchases make it so.*
segments.tr: يمكن أن يكون استثماراً سليماً إذا اشترى هؤلاء العملاء مرة أخرى، لكن فقط عمليات الشراء المتكررة تجعلها كذلك.*

fr.title: [Marketing 101 #12] Pourquoi cette pub vous a trouvé dix secondes après votre recherche

segments.src: > Digital marketing isn't one thing — it's three different jobs: social media goes where attention already is, search advertising catches demand at the exact moment someone types it, and content marketing earns trust long before anyone is ready to buy.
segments.tr: > Le marketing numérique n'est pas une seule chose — c'est trois emplois différents : les réseaux sociaux vont là où l'attention existe déjà, la publicité de recherche capture la demande au moment exact où quelqu'un la tape, et le marketing de contenu gagne la confiance longtemps avant que quelqu'un soit prêt à acheter.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: Most people picture "digital marketing" as a single blob of ads on the internet.
segments.tr: La plupart des gens imaginent le « marketing numérique » comme une seule masse d'annonces sur Internet.

segments.src: It's more useful to think of it as three distinct jobs, each answering a different question about the customer.
segments.tr: Il est plus utile de le voir comme trois emplois distincts, chacun répondant à une question différente sur le client.

segments.src: **Social media marketing** answers: *how do we reach people who aren't looking for us yet?* On Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, or Reddit, nobody opened the app to shop.
segments.tr: **Le marketing sur les réseaux sociaux** répond à : *comment atteindre les gens qui ne nous recherchent pas encore ?* Sur Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn ou Reddit, personne n'a ouvert l'application pour faire du shopping.

segments.src: They came for entertainment or connection.
segments.tr: Ils sont venus pour le divertissement ou la connexion.

segments.src: So the ad has to earn its place in the feed — it interrupts.
segments.tr: Donc l'annonce doit gagner sa place dans le flux — elle interrompt.

segments.src: That means you pay for **attention** and target by *who someone is* (age, location, interests, past behavior, lookalikes of your existing customers).
segments.tr: Cela signifie que vous payez pour l'**attention** et ciblez par *qui est quelqu'un* (âge, localisation, intérêts, comportement passé, lookalikes de vos clients existants).

segments.src: Demand here is **latent**: you're creating want that wasn't there five seconds ago.
segments.tr: La demande ici est **latente** : vous créez un besoin qui n'existait pas il y a cinq secondes.

segments.src: **Search advertising** answers: *how do we show up when someone is already looking?* Someone types "emergency plumber Chicago" into Google.
segments.tr: **La publicité de recherche** répond à : *comment apparaître quand quelqu'un cherche déjà ?* Quelqu'un tape « plombier d'urgence Chicago » dans Google.

segments.src: They have a problem right now.
segments.tr: Ils ont un problème maintenant.

segments.src: You're not creating demand — you're **harvesting** it.
segments.tr: Vous ne créez pas la demande — vous la **récoltez**.

segments.src: That's why search clicks convert far better than social clicks, and why they cost more.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi les clics de recherche se convertissent beaucoup mieux que les clics sociaux, et pourquoi ils coûtent plus cher.

segments.src: Here's the part most beginners get wrong: search ads are not a simple "highest bidder wins" auction.
segments.tr: Voici la partie que la plupart des débutants se trompent : les annonces de recherche ne sont pas une simple enchère « le plus offrant gagne ».

segments.src: Google and Bing rank ads roughly by a combination of your bid and how relevant and useful your ad and landing page are (Google calls its relevance signal **Quality Score**).
segments.tr: Google et Bing classent les annonces à peu près en fonction d'une combinaison de votre enchère et de la pertinence et de l'utilité de votre annonce et de votre page de destination (Google appelle son signal de pertinence **Quality Score**).

segments.src: Simplified:
segments.tr: Simplifié :

segments.src: Ad Rank ≈ Max Bid × Quality Score (plus other context signals)
segments.tr: Ad Rank ≈ Max Bid × Quality Score (plus other context signals)

segments.src: The practical consequence: a well-written ad pointing to a fast, relevant landing page can outrank a competitor who bids more.
segments.tr: La conséquence pratique : une annonce bien écrite pointant vers une page de destination rapide et pertinente peut surclasser un concurrent qui enchérit davantage.

segments.src: Relevance is a discount.
segments.tr: La pertinence est une réduction.

segments.src: **Content marketing** answers: *how do we get chosen when someone finally compares options?* Blog posts, comparison guides, newsletters, YouTube explainers, podcasts.
segments.tr: **Le marketing de contenu** répond à : *comment se faire choisir quand quelqu'un compare enfin les options ?* Articles de blog, guides de comparaison, infolettres, explications YouTube, podcasts.

segments.src: You're not selling — you're being useful.
segments.tr: Vous ne vendez pas — vous êtes utile.

segments.src: The payoff is slow and compounding: an article that ranks in search or gets shared keeps working for months or years after you publish it, with no per-click cost.
segments.tr: La récompense est lente et composée : un article qui se classe dans la recherche ou qui est partagé continue de fonctionner pendant des mois ou des années après sa publication, sans coût par clic.

segments.src: The tradeoff is that it takes time to build and is hard to attribute cleanly.
segments.tr: L'inconvénient est que cela prend du temps à construire et est difficile à attribuer proprement.

segments.src: A common way to organize all three is the **paid / owned / earned** framework:
segments.tr: Un moyen courant d'organiser les trois est le framework **payant / propriétaire / gagné** :

segments.src: - **Paid** — you rent the audience (social ads, search ads). Fast, measurable, stops the moment you stop paying.
segments.tr: - **Payant** — vous louez l'audience (annonces sociales, annonces de recherche). Rapide, mesurable, s'arrête au moment où vous arrêtez de payer.

segments.src: - **Owned** — you control the asset (your website, blog, email list, app). Slow to build, but it's yours.
segments.tr: - **Propriétaire** — vous contrôlez l'actif (votre site Web, blog, liste de diffusion, application). Lent à construire, mais c'est le vôtre.

segments.src: - **Earned** — others give it to you (word of mouth, press, reviews, shares). Most credible, least controllable.
segments.tr: - **Gagné** — d'autres vous le donnent (bouche à oreille, presse, avis, partages). Plus crédible, moins contrôlable.

segments.src: Healthy programs use all three.
segments.tr: Les programmes sains utilisent les trois.

segments.src: Paid buys you speed; owned buys you independence from ad costs; earned buys you credibility neither of the others can purchase directly.
segments.tr: Le payant vous achète de la rapidité ; le propriétaire vous achète l'indépendance des coûts publicitaires ; le gagné vous achète la crédibilité qu'aucun des deux autres ne peut acheter directement.
